title: Inertial Sense SDK data sets (src/data_sets.h)
license_line: struct member names, types and array sizes only; MIT License
extra_sources: Inertial Sense SDK src/ISComm.h at the same commit: the ISB packet header (preamble, flags, data id, payload size); the frame and its checksum are the framer's
byte_order_statement: little-endian, as the file header of data_sets.h states for every multi-byte field

frame.name: ISB packet header

fields.name: flags, extended payload and offset bits (high nibble)

convention: A message of this format is one ISB (Inertial Sense binary) packet without its trailing
2-byte checksum: the 6-byte packet header of `src/ISComm.h` (`packet_hdr_t`), then the whole
data set the header's id names. The header starts with the preamble 0x49EF (bytes EF 49),
then a flags byte whose low nibble is the packet type (4 for a data packet, 5 for a set-data
packet), the data id (the DID number) and the payload size in bytes. Each DID is a kind,
selected by its id and by a payload size equal to its struct. The checksum after the payload
is the framer's: the ISB parser of the SDK (`is_comm_parse` in `src/ISComm.c`, with
`is_comm_isb_checksum16`) checks and strips it, and writes it when it sends. A packet with
the offset flag (0x20, a partial data set) or the extended-payload flag (0x10) is not a
message of this format; the common `when` on the high nibble refuses it.

skip.DID_INL2_COVARIANCE_LD: its payload is named by an array size, not a struct: a bare array of floats the header declares no type for
skip.DID_INL2_MISC: the header names `inl2_misc_t` as its payload but declares no such type
skip.DID_FIRMWARE_UPDATE: the header names `firmware_payload_t` as its payload but declares no such type
skip.DID_GNSS_BASE_RAW: `gnss_raw_t` holds a union (`uGnssRawData`) whose bytes are observations, ephemerides or other records by a type field; one fixed layout cannot state them
skip.DID_EVB_FLASH_CFG: `evb_server_t` holds an anonymous union (an IP address as one word or four bytes), which the strict reader does not lay out

bind_note: The three elements of `lla` are bound where the struct's comment states WGS 84 latitude and
longitude in degrees and the height above the ellipsoid in metres (the file header says the
same of every LLA). `ins_4_t` (ECEF) and the NED offset of `ins_1_t` are not positions in
degrees and stay raw keys. No struct states a velocity in NED without a condition: the INS
`uvw` is in the body frame, and `gnss_vel_t.vel` is ECEF or north-east by a status bit, so
no velocity is bound. Times are GPS week and time of week, not UTC epoch times, and stay raw.
